title: Match a verb to its subject
objective: Find the main noun and choose the matching verb.

slides.title: Find the main noun first
body: The main noun tells you whether the subject is singular or plural. A nearby noun can distract you.
Try covering the phrase that begins with of or on.

slides.title: Compare two subjects
body: “The colour of the leaves changes.” The main noun is colour, so use changes.
“The leaves on the branch change.” The main noun is leaves, so use change.
Read the shorter sentences aloud: “The colour changes.” “The leaves change.”

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: A group of snails ___ (live/lives) here. The shells on the table ___ (look/looks) smooth.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Find the subject head noun in each sentence.
Use singular agreement for “group”. Choose both verbs.
Ignore the phrase after of, on or in.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: A group of bees ___ (visit/visits) here. The flowers in the park ___ (look/looks) bright.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Find the subject head noun in each sentence.
Use singular agreement for “group”. Choose both verbs.
Rewrite the second sentence with a singular subject.

slides.title: Change one noun
body: Make your subject singular, then plural. Read both sentences to a partner and point to the verb that changes.
